title: Jewelry worth millions of dollars stolen from French museum in daring early-morning raid
facts: Burglars broke into the Lalique museum in Wingen-sur-Moder, France, around 5:30 am on a Sunday.
Thieves smashed open six display cases inside the Lalique museum's jewelry room.
Approximately 20 pieces of jewelry were stolen from the Lalique museum during the burglary.
The estimated value of the stolen Lalique museum jewelry is close to four million euros.
The jewelry stolen from the Lalique museum was made of crystal without precious gems.
A cleaning lady was the first person to arrive at the Lalique museum after the burglary and called the police.
The Lalique museum, dedicated to jeweler and glassmaker Rene Lalique, opened in 2011.
The Lalique museum houses more than 650 works of Art Nouveau jewelry, Art Deco glass, and contemporary crystal.
The town of Wingen-sur-Moder has a population of approximately 1,500 inhabitants.
Thieves stole $102 million worth of jewelry from the Louvre museum in Paris in October 2025.
A security audit determined that 35% of the rooms in the Louvre's Denon Wing were not monitored by security cameras during the 2025 heist.
A woman was arrested and charged in October 2025 for stealing gold from the Natural History Museum in Paris.
Thieves stole three porcelain works from the Adrien Dubouche National Museum in Limoges in September 2025.
Four men smashed display cases at the Cognacq-Jay museum in Paris in November 2024 to steal 18th-century works.
The 2024 Cognacq-Jay museum heist resulted in a $4 million insurance payment to the Royal Collection Trust.
